title: CRLR/424/2019 of KRISHAN KUMAR VERMA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision (CRLR No. 424 of 2019)
Krishan Kumar Verma .....Revisionist
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and another ...Respondents
Advocate : Mr. Vaibhav Pandit, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. P.S. Bohra, AGA for the State of Uttarakhand.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Though hesitatingly, but the circumstances, as it has been
observed by the learned counsel for the revisionist during the course of
argument calls for invoking the powers of this Court as vested under
Section 401 of the Cr.P.C. by this Court, while considering the present
revision, which involve peculiar circumstances of the case.
2. In a criminal proceedings which was registered as Criminal
Case No. 158 of 2013 (old case No. 160 of 2011), Amit Kumar v.
Marshall Construction Unit and Another, a proceeding under Section 138
of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881, was drawn as against the present
revisionist and ultimately by the impugned order dated 18th May 2016, he
was convicted by the Court of 2nd Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Dehradun and he was directed to undergo a simple imprisonment for a
period of 1 year and he was also directed to furnish a penalty of Rs.
50,00,000/- (Rupees Fifty Lakh only) within a period of 1 month from
the date of the order.
3. As against the order of conviction dated 18th May 2016, the
revisionist contends that he has preferred a Criminal Appeal before the
Fifth Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun, which has been numbered as
Criminal Appeal Number 87 of 2016, Krishan Kumar v. Amit. When the
Appeal was entertained, the learned Appellate Court, while considering
the Application paper number 6 (kha), which was presented by the
appellant before the Fifth Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun had
passed a conditional order, whereby granting the stay of the execution of
the sentence on the fulfilment of a condition of extension of a bank

2
guarantee for an amount of Rs. 25,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakh
only) by an order dated 9th June 2016 as passed by the Appellate Court.
4. It is the case of the revisionist that in compliance of the
order dated 9th June 2016, he did furnish the bank guarantee for the said
amount, but the bank guarantee, as furnished by him expired
approximately in the month of February 2018. He submits that in the
meantime the bank guarantee could not be extended on account of the
fact that he was later on diagnosed to be suffering from chronic liver
cirrhosis, for which he was undergoing treatment and his mobility was
also completely hampered. Thus in order to defend his arrest in
pursuance to the order of conviction and also because of the expiry of the
term of bank guarantee as extended by the revisionist, he had moved an
application before the Appellate Court being Application No. 55B to the
effect that the period of the bank guarantee, which has expired, he may be
granted a reasonable time period for extension of the bank guarantee and
in order to renew the same, he may be granted a reasonable time as the
Court may deem fit considering the ailment, with which the revisionist
was suffering.
5. The said application paper number 55B, which was filed by
the revisionist on 4th March 2019, was supported with an affidavit paper
number 54B along with the documents of his medical treatment, which
was being carried in the Max Hospital, Dehradun. The said application
came up for consideration before the Court of Fifth Additional Sessions
Judge, Dehradun, and the Court by virtue of an order dated 26th April
2019, the Court has rejected the Application on the ground that the bank
guarantee which was supposed to be renewed by him since was not
renewed in time, he can not avail the benefit of the protection granted by
the order dated 9th June 2016.
6. The contention of the learned counsel for the revisionist
before this Court is that looking to the pathetic physical condition of the
revisionist, even the Sessions Court has transferred the proceedings of

3
Appeal No. 87 of 2016, Krishan Kumar v. Amit from the second floor to
the ground floor by an order dated 3rd July 2019.
7. The learned counsel for the revisionist submits that in
compliance of an order for furnishing the bank guarantee as directed by
the order dated 9th June 2016, the period of which has expired in 2018, he
undertakes to furnish the guarantee in relation to the amount as directed
by the order dated 9th June 2016, for which the revisionist wants to seek a
reasonable time of about three months to furnish the guarantee or to
extend the guarantee which was already given by the revisionist.
8. The period as prayed for by the revisionist is on much higher
side, on considering the material which has been brought on record, this
Court is of the view that considering the pathetic health condition and
also simultaneously maintaining an equitable balance from the viewpoint
that, admittedly, he happens to be a convict for commission of the
offences under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881,
wherein he has been made responsible to remit a amount of Rs. 50.00
lakh as penalty, this Court taking compassionate view this Court is of the
view that two months time only would be reasonable for the revisionist to
either get the guarantee extended, which had been expired in the month
February 2018, or furnish a fresh guarantee in relation to a sum of Rs.
25.00 lakh as directed by the order dated 9th June 2016.
9. Subject to the aforesaid observation, this revision is being
disposed of and for a period of two months, the warrant, which has been
issued as against the revisionist, would be kept in abeyance.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 30.07.2019
Mahinder/
